questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic opportunities offered at the university, along with the nature and sports opportunities that exists in the country. The university is highly ranked in Australia and it was interestereting to experience my degree in english and in another country. Furthermore, the country has amazing nature, and opportunities for activities that we don't have in Denmark, such as surfing. The fact that the country is difficult to visit due to its placement, was also something that made me want to got her for exchange. Lastly, I wanted to challenge myself by living in a whole new country alone.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to covid-19 almost all of my classes were online. This made the social aspects of the exchange more difficult, as I didn't meet many people in the university. It required a lot of extra effort to meet people outside of the university. Furthermore, I couldn't find any study groups in my classes, and thus I couldn't share ideas or study together with other students in the classes. As I was completely new to the university and the way of teaching, this made the beginning of the exchange stay challenging.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university had introduction days which provided a lot of necessary information. These included basic information on the campus and on the university's social clubs for students. Though the introduction was good, I still had trouble to know where to seek  help if if I had questions regarding my courses later on in the stay. This meant that I wrote emails directly to the professors of my classes, which might have resulted in extra unnecessary work for them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introduction days mentioned above. There was no extra assistance upon arrival. I believe that it would have been beneficial to provide exchange students with a "buddy-student" from the university, who could help the exchange students to start up the courses. It was difficult to navigate physically on campus, and even more difficult to navigate on the teaching platforms used for online classes and assignments. I would have appreciated to have a contact person, who was an existing student on the university, that I could ask practical questions in relation to studying.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Though I found the navigating physically on campus and online on the teaching platorms difficult, I still found the orientation in the introduction days beneficial and succesfull. Going on exchange it is expected that you have to spend some time and effort in order to get familiar with the teaching methods and the areas, so I think it would be difficult to completely avoid that. However, I think that future exchange students would benefit a lot from a "buddy-student" from the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find a housing in Sydney, as the prices are very high in Australia. My boyfriend had been on exchange on the same university a couple of years ago, so he had the contact information of a house, where I could rent a room for a reasonable price. However, people without connections in the city, had to use social media platforms such as Facebook to find rooms for rental, which usually were vastly overpriced.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Future students should be aware that housing in Sydney is extremely expensive. It takes time and effort to find rooms for rent for a reasonable price, and students should check social media platforms such as Facebook and
Flatmates.com
well ahead of time, to ensure a proper housing. Living on campus is a good choice if you're going alone as an exchange student, as you'll be sure to live with other exchange students, with whom you can consult in regards to practical studying questions. Furthermore, it is an easy way to socialize and meet friends who are in the same situation as you. When living off campus, there's a risk that you dont have anything in common with the other residents, which might result in no socializing. In most cases, I would therefore recommend to live on campus, or reach out to previous exchange students at the university for contact information on good housing options off campus. The only drawback by living on campus is the fact that it is very expensive. Living on campus can exceed the costs of living off campus by a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The opportunity for socializing with other students when living on campus was excellent. However, the price was way too expensive. Help to find housing off campus was non-existing, resulting in a stressfull experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As the university hosts exchange students from the University of Copenhagen every year, I thought that the registration would be fairly easy and straightforward. However, registering at the university along with finding relevant courses that could be approved by the University of Copenhagen required a lot of effort and time. Future students should be aware that they need to set aside a lot of time besides their studying and student jobs at home, for this process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Finding courses in my degree was difficult, due to the university's semester structure. The university has a three semester-structure, which means that exchange students need to take an intense three-week course before the actual semester begin, in order to obtain enough ECTS-points. Furthermore, the point-system obtained from the courses was not the same in for the University of Copenhagen, and the points had to be converted. I spent a lot of time and effort on finding new and relevant courses, that did not overlap with courses I had previously received at the University of Copenhagen, by thoroughly reading the course information of the different courses offered.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university had an email address that you could write to. However, due to the time difference and the fact that they got a lot of emails from students, the response-time was very long. This made the process stressfull, as registration had to be done within certain deadlines. I would suggest the university to offer "buddy-students" from the university to all future exchange students. This would have been an extremely helpful thing, that would have made the experience way less stressfull. In my own case I contacted all the students from the University of Copenhagen who were going to the same university as myself during the application process, so that we could socialize and help each other with practical questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeeded in my registration of classes. The was however due to the fact that I could consult with my brother and boyfriend, who had both been on exchange in Australia previously. Furthermore, I began well ahead of time, which I would recommend all future exchange students to do.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To ask previous students that's been on exchange on the university for help, and to begin the process well ahead of time. Furthermore, it's important to set aside plenty of time for the process, as it is more time consuming than one might might think initially.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The content of the courses was very rewarding and interesting. However, the fact that almost all of my courses were online, made the academic experience more challenging. It was difficult to follow the courses online, as I didn't have previous experience with the platforms used. This impacted my the academic experience negatively. Because of the online delivery there was no opportunity to initiate study groups, which would have been extremely helpful.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
They were high level, and required much effort. Due to the exam structure of the university, where each course is divided into two or three exams taken throughout the semester, it was important to attend all lectures and tutorials. There was not time to study for the fina exam, as I'm used to at the University of Copenhagen. 
I would say that I used more time studying during my exchange, than I do at my home university. This I think can also be explained by a general lack of working in study groups, which I find very beneficial at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was similar to the teaching style at the University of Copenhagen. However, there were more lectures and less tutorials. This meant that I had to do more studying on my own than I'm used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHCM9012 Health Promotion & Social Perspectives of Health, PHCM9050 Immunisation Policy and Practice, PHCM9786 Global approaches to Cardiovascular Disease, Diabetes & Cancer Prevention, BEES6601
An Introduction to the Sydney Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BEES6601 An Introduction to the Sydney Environment. Though this was an introduction course, that only lasted three weeks, it was the only course where I met other students as it was fully physical. The course was meant as an introduction for all exchange students, and it gave me a crucial introduction to studying at the university overall. It was a perfect introduction, and I really recommend all exchange students to take this course. The content of the course was not as interesting for my degree, as my other courses. However, it introduced me to the social, physical and historical context to Sydney, which made the exchange a lot more interesting for me. The professors were extremely helpful, and the course was a great experience.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter many costs that I hadn't expected. However, several of the costs were way higher than I had anticipated. The only unexpected cost was the one of the student visa, which was very high. Future students should be aware of this cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The costs of flight tickets from Denmark to Sydney and return, was a lot more expensive than I expected. I bought the tickets well ahead of time, and it was still very expensive. Furthermore, the costs of phone and internet, as well as public transportation were high. I bought a used bicycle upon my arrival, which significantly lowered the costs of public transportation. However, many buses and trams didn't operate at night, resulting in quite expensive taxi and Uber costs. Biking at night is not recommended, as there are no bicycle lanes, and people drive very close and fast to cyclists.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university offered many social clubs for the students. However, registration in the clubs was difficult, and I couldn't figure out the systems, as well as when and where the different clubs met. This meant that I didn't participate in any social clubs offered at the university. A solution to this would again be to have a "buddy-student" at the university, who could help registering for the clubs. This would have helped me a lot.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offered more than 200 different clubs. This included sports, academic and other kinds of clubs, such as cooking cubs and clubs where you could learn new languages. I was impressed y the amount of different clubs offered at the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend students to join sports clubs, such as the outdoor basketball or surfing club. This allows you to meet other students, as well as take advantage of the beautiful and unique nature, that Sydney has. The people I know, who participated in these clubs met a lot of friends in this way - both from the university, and other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend future students to travel around the area. There's a lot of national parks and beaches close to Sydney that are very beautiful and easy to reach by train, bus or car. Plan and structure your studies, so that you have time to travel and explore the area. In the longer holidays, most students leave Sydney, and this is a great opportunity to go on a longer trip, eg. travelling the coast or other parts of Australia. I recommend taking advantage of the fact that you are a place in the world, that is difficult to reach, and that most people don't get to see.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very similar to the culture in Denmark. The only significant difference is the alcohol culture, as beers etc. are way more expensive in Australia compared to Denmark. However, there's still plenty of social gatherings and parties, so this is not a problem for the overall experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the first days of school (introduction). This offers a lot of social events and important information. It's nice to know other exchange students, as you probably face some of the same challenges, and in this way you can help each other. Furthermore, I recommend joining some of the social clubs to meet local students, as local students use the clubs a lot. Lastly, it's important not to live alone. The easiest way to meet new friends is to live at campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find adapting to the culture challenging at all. People in Australia are in general very ope and helpfull, so this was not a problem at all.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the opportunities for surfing, and the nature surrounding Sydney. This is very unique, and I highly recommend future students to take advantage of this.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Set aside plenty of time to find good and social housing. This might mean that you have to reach out to previous exchange students for help, or spend a lot of time on social platforms such as Facebook or
Flatmate.com
. However, a good housing is fundamental to the experience. 2. It's also important to attend classes, as there are examinations throughout the whole semester. If you want to have time to explore the area and travel, you have to plan and structure your studies from the beginning. 3. Make sure that you have money saved up. The cost of they stay is very high, and you have to be prepared to pay a lot for housing, insurance, visa and flight tickets.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: One of the most important things is to reach out to a previous exchange student at the university. Make sure you have someone from the University of Copenhagen, who has been on exchange on the same university, that you can contact regarding practical questions.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me, the most rewarding part was to experience the nature and surfing opportunities, as well as getting new friends. However, I also found it very exciting to experience my degree in another country, and to be able to compare the similarities and differences in the public health degree, when delivered in Sydney compared to Denmark. The academic content was extremely rewarding and unique.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The most challenging part was navigating on campus and the university's course structure, as well as getting familiar with the platforms for online lectures, tutorials and exams. I hope future students will have physical attendance in their courses, as I believe this would have made both the academic and social aspects of the exchange easier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Exchange is a wonderful experience, that I will remember for the rest of my life. It has been extremely rewarding both socially, personally and academically. I would recommend it to everyone.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
